etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From Middle English away, awey, awei, oway, o wey, on way, from Old English āweġ, onweġ (“away”), originally on weġ (“on one's way; onward; on”), equivalent to a- (“on”) +‎ way.

Cognate with Scots awa, away (“away”), Old Frisian aweg, awei (“away”), Saterland Frisian wäch, wääge (“away”), Dutch weg (“away”), German weg (“away”), Danish væk (“away”), Swedish i väg (“away; off; along”).

definitions.definition: From a place, hence.

quote.citation: 1921, Ben Travers, chapter 5, in A Cuckoo in the Nest, Garden City, N.Y.: Doubleday, Page & Company, published 1925, →OCLC:
quote.text: The departure was not unduly prolonged. […] Within the door Mrs. Spoker hastily imparted to Mrs. Love a few final sentiments […] ; a deep, guttural instigation to the horse; and the wheels of the waggonette crunched heavily away into obscurity.

quote.citation: 2014 June 14, “It's a gas”, in The Economist, volume 411, number 8891:
quote.text: One of the hidden glories of Victorian engineering is proper drains. Isolating a city’s effluent and shipping it away in underground sewers has probably saved more lives than any medical procedure except vaccination.

definitions.definition: Aside; off; in another direction.
Aside, so as to discard something.
At a stated distance in time or space.

quote.citation: 1948, Carey McWilliams, North from Mexico / The Spanish-Speaking People of The United States, J. B. Lippincott Company, page 25:
quote.text: While De Anza was exploring the Bay of San Francisco, seeking a site for the presidio, the American colonists on the eastern seaboard, three thousand miles away, were celebrating the signing of the Declaration of Independence.

quote.citation: 2013 June 8, “The new masters and commanders”, in The Economist, volume 407, number 8839, page 52:
quote.text: From the ground, Colombo’s port does not look like much. Those entering it are greeted by wire fences, walls dating back to colonial times and security posts. For mariners leaving the port after lonely nights on the high seas, the delights of the B52 Night Club and Stallion Pub lie a stumble away.

definitions.definition: In or to something's usual or proper storage place.
In or to a secure or out-of-the-way place.
From a state or condition of being; out of existence.
So as to remove or use up something.
(as imperative, by ellipsis) Come away; go away; take away.

quote.citation: 1933+, Fran Striker, The Lone Ranger, WXYZ-AM

definitions.definition: On; in continuance; without intermission or delay.
Without restraint.
(Can we verify(+) this sense?) (Northern England) Come on! Go on!
(Scotland, dismissal) Away with you! Go away!
Not here, gone, absent, unavailable, traveling; on vacation.
At a specified distance in space, time, or figuratively.
(chiefly sports) Not on one's home territory.
(baseball, following the noun modified) Out.
(golf) Being the player whose ball lies farthest from the hole (or, in disc golf, whose disc lies farthest from the target).

quote.citation: 2016, Justin Menickelli, Ryan Pickens, Definitive Guide to Disc Golf:
quote.text: For example, immediately after every person in the group has teed off, if you are clearly the away player (perhaps because you smacked your drive into the tree closest to the tee pad), you should grab your bag and try to be the first person advancing down the fairway.

definitions.definition: (intransitive, poetic) To depart; to go to another place.
Misspelling of aweigh.
